output:
NO-GO — the plan is not ready for implementation. I made no file or branch changes.

The selected lenses were data migration and reversibility, API/Web contract evolution, Mobile compatibility, and repository delivery safety. The lens questions were reviewed separately because each owns different evidence. Codex could not start fresh child contexts because the available agent threads were exhausted, so these were moderator-only passes; evidence coverage is complete, but independent-subagent validation is degraded.

| Severity | Evidence-backed finding | Required correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BLOCKER | Plan step 1 adds a non-null `VARCHAR(5)`, while the known state has 2.4 million existing profiles and explicitly lacks a backfill and migration timing. The plan does not define a valid value for existing rows or a safe way to enforce the constraint. | Decide the existing-profile and absent-value semantics, use an additive compatible state first (nullable or an explicitly approved default), backfill in bounded batches, verify completion, rehearse on production-scale data, and enforce non-null only after measured lock/latency gates pass. |
| BLOCKER | Plan steps 2 and 4 expose the API change before Mobile is updated, while supported Mobile v4 clients reject unknown enum values and no compatibility rollout exists. The plan has no control that prevents an unsupported value from reaching those clients. | Define the supported language-tag set and compatibility matrix, update or capability-gate Mobile before emitting new values, retain a backward-compatible response during the support window, and prove old/new behavior with contract tests. |
| HIGH | Plan step 2 couples the database migration and API response change even though the authoritative API contract currently omits the optional field, and no contract test is specified. A single coupled release removes the safe observation and rollback boundary between storage and consumers. | Use an expand/contract rollout: deploy compatible storage first, update the API contract additively, deploy tolerant Web/API behavior behind a controlled rollout, observe it, and only later tighten invariants. Add contract tests for omitted, present, known, and unsupported values. |
| HIGH | Plan step 5 rolls back by dropping the column, and the fixture explicitly says there is no rollback-data policy. Once profiles have written preferences, that rollback destroys user data. | Make the operational rollback disable writes and response exposure while preserving the column. Define retention, export/recovery, ownership, and verification before any later destructive cleanup. |
| HIGH | The known repository state is `main` with an unrelated dirty edit owned by another workstream; repository instructions require material work on a feature branch and forbid stashing or overwriting that edit. Implementation in the current workspace would violate an explicit authority. | Before implementation, establish an authorized isolated feature-branch workspace from the correct revision, recheck status and ownership, and leave the current dirty worktree untouched. Do not create or switch branches during this read-only review. |

The genuine product decision is the meaning of `preferred_language` for existing or unset profiles, including the allowed tag set and whether absence remains valid. The remaining corrections are engineering plan work, not additional approval gates.

Re-run readiness review only after the revised plan includes the data semantics, staged migration and rollout, Mobile support strategy, non-destructive rollback policy, production-scale timing and abort thresholds, contract/migration tests, observability and owners, and a safe branch/worktree procedure. Until then, the gate remains NO-GO.
